cards.title: Produce one deterministic global top-three list

interview_practice.scope: Sourced interview-design questions and interview practice only.

cards.review_practice_examples_note: These prompts are curriculum explain-backs, not claims about actual company interview questions. System-design practice uses only the sourced separate question bank and the existing allocated block.
cards.architecture_explanation: Sort one global candidate score map by support descending and exact media ID ascending; take at most K=3. The result does not depend on viewer history, holdout data, randomness, or adaptive K.

cards.title: Build the evaluation cohort without deleting difficult targets
cards.review_practice_examples_note: These prompts are curriculum explain-backs, not claims about actual company interview questions. System-design practice uses only the sourced separate question bank and the existing allocated block.
cards.architecture_explanation: Group distinct positive holdout targets by viewer while separately retaining every observed viewer and zero-positive count. Do not intersect targets with candidates, because dropping unreachable positives would inflate recall.

cards.title: Compute one viewer’s fixed-slot precision and recall

interview_practice.scope: Sourced interview-design questions and interview practice only.

cards.review_practice_examples_note: These prompts are curriculum explain-backs, not claims about actual company interview questions. System-design practice uses only the sourced separate question bank and the existing allocated block.
cards.architecture_explanation: Count each hit once; precision uses the fixed denominator 3 even for a short result, while recall divides by the distinct positive target count. Empty-target cases are explicitly non-evaluable.

cards.architecture_explanation: This recovery day uses only Days 169–174 selectors: repair the first unresolved seam and repeat an independent counterexample. Do not add later comparison, report, or CLI work.

cards.title: Aggregate macro metrics with explicit coverage counts
cards.review_practice_examples_note: These prompts are curriculum explain-backs, not claims about actual company interview questions. System-design practice uses only the sourced separate question bank and the existing allocated block.
cards.architecture_explanation: Reuse the per-viewer scorer, macro-average positive-target viewers without weighting, and publish cohort and reachability counts beside the metrics. Determine cold start from every training interaction, including zero-watch events.

cards.architecture_explanation: Compare popularity and the fixed ascending-ID reference with identical candidates, targets, K, and cohort. Return both measurements and signed deltas; do not choose a winner or tune on holdout.

prior_readiness_gate.name: Days 153–154 learner-owned A/B evidence

qualifying_evidence.source_identity: tested_source_sha is a 40-character hexadecimal commit SHA
qualifying_evidence.artifacts: at least two distinct SHA-256 artifact hashes with explicit baseline/candidate roles
qualifying_evidence.execution: record the exact matrix selector and matrix_exit_code 0
qualifying_evidence.provenance: record baseline and candidate source identities and build recipes; include any temporary witness provenance
qualifying_evidence.result_and_limits: record observed matrix result and proof_limits

prior_readiness_gate.required_evidence: Learner-owned run of the Day 153/154 A/B matrix, distinct baseline/candidate artifacts with hashes, tested source identity, source/overlay provenance, successful exact matrix selector, observed result, and proof limits.
prior_readiness_gate.rule: A starter or assistant/instructor witness cannot satisfy this gate. Keep StreamForge progression/completion claims blocked until the authoritative Day 153 and Day 154 learner evidence records satisfy the qualifying-evidence contract. Re-evaluate these records when genuine learner evidence is added; do not freeze the gate as permanently unmet.
